title: Durable reactive CO2 capture exceeding 1,000 h via self-reinforcing molecular catalysts - Nature Energy
text:
AbstractElectrochemical carbon dioxide (CO2) reduction using low-carbon electricity provides a means to decarbonize chemical and fuel production. However, CO2 reduction typically requires high-purity CO2 obtained through capture and subsequent energy-intensive regeneration. Reactive capture integrates CO2 capture and conversion, avoiding the desorption step, but existing systems show poor durability. Here we show that the pH swing intrinsic to reactive-capture systems drives protons towards the cathode, creating an acidic microenvironment that accelerates catalyst demetallation. To address this, we construct a covalently linked cobalt (Co) phthalocyanine catalyst supported on carbon nanotubes, in which early ~50% Co leaching generates vacancies and induces cooperative contraction of neighbouring Co sites, strengthening Co–N coordination and suppressing further demetallation. The resulting self-reinforcing vacancy–network interaction enables continuous operation for over 1,000 h at 50 mA cm−2 with ~80% carbon monoxide Faradaic efficiency and 39% energy efficiency at 2.9 V. These findings provide a pathway towards robust molecular catalysts for reactive carbon capture and electrochemical conversion.
